anchor.subject: cinematic grandiose hero shot of Ember Mesa at dusk, movie-poster composition, a sand desert first: big salmon dunes spill over the half-buried ruins of an abandoned futuristic mega-city. Foreground: sand-drifted debris, a broken mag-rail beam and the crest of a dune. Down the middle runs Bolt's path, a ruined avenue drifted with rippled sand, cracked dark paving and a collapsed mag-rail line half under the sand, its leading lines converging on the landmark spire. Mid-ground: colossal broken towers and skyscraper shells dwarf the avenue on both sides, a broken sky-bridge spans it, a giant fallen starship hull lies buried in a dune, dead holographic sign frames, a few small amber lights still flickering; layered sandstone mesas and a natural sandstone arch still frame the city. At the end of the avenue the city's landmark beacon: a tall dark basalt and brushed-metal signal spire behind the arch, two thin floating rings glowing warm amber, a faint beam to the sky. Far: the ruined city stretches to the horizon, tower silhouettes fading layer after layer into warm atmospheric haze. The low sun on the right backlights the ruins with bright rim light on every edge and long god-rays through the gaps between the towers. In the violet sky thin planetary ring arcs, a small pale second moon and faint stars near the zenith

tone.$note: free tone words for this biome (local only)
tone.layoutNote: SmiR 2026-10-08: zone B is a FREE-ROAM 360 degree mega-city, not a corridor. The avenue is only the main street. Districts (dune-buried avenue, tower canyon, fallen spaceport, mesa gate, spire plaza) connect in all directions; no invisible walls, collisions follow real geometry; the spire is the landmark seen from everywhere.
tone.skyNote: 2026-10-08 (SmiR via review of sky v1): sky plates are SKY ONLY (gradient, clouds, sun at azimuth 90, faint stars near the zenith, a haze band at the horizon in the key's haze colour; below the horizon a flat haze band hidden by the ground mesh). The city skyline at the horizon is real 3D low-LOD tower solids from the city kit placed in the fog band (objects group). The ring arc and the small second moon are 3D meshes like the planet (a ring band mesh + a moon sphere, Imagine or plate-derived textures later). Never paint towers, rings or moons into sky plates.
tone.skyV2Note: 2026-10-08 sky v2 built (not baked, not wired): plates tools/biome/out/ember-mesa/sky-in3 (H1-H5) + sky-in4/sky-H0 (sun-up retry), Z/N reused from v1 (sky-final-norm/sky-Z, sky-final/sky-N). Imagine kept the sun on the horizon twice although asked for 8 deg up, so H0's own sun glow was moved up 8 deg in post (zb-bible-1008/tools/sun_lift.py, Imagine pixels only) -> sky-in5. Clean-up zb-bible-1008/tools/sky_prep.py -> sky-final2: re-level horizons to mid-height, common gradient profile, per-plate L-R flatten (no domes), haze band graded onto the key haze with the anti-sun drop qc.horizonAntiSunDL, overlap seam match, below-horizon = flat haze band, Z flat-fielded to the plate tops, N flat sand haze. Stitch: stitch_sky.py --no-flatten --no-align -> out/ember-mesa/sky2. Fog write-back NOT done yet (sampled horizon #c79680, nearHaze #bd8c7f, farCool #8a7791).
tone.groundNote: 2026-10-08 ground group v1 (not baked, not wired): Imagine plates ground-in (g1,g5,g6,g7), ground-in2 (g3, g4 v2 'slope below the crest', the first g4 had one diagonal crest band), ground-in3 (g0 v2 calm base layer), ground-in4 (g2 v2, the first had diagonal sand bands that read as a grid).
